# Regulatory Compliance Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Regulatory Compliance Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 26 captured build checkpoints; 5 skills; 2 knowledge files; 8 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access. Confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available; keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, the proposed connections and the channel; document blocked paths rather than bypassing them. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always authentication trigger; record who may build, test and use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for trade and reporting data, the ARM, the learning management system and Teams, each with a dedicated least-privilege reference. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare compliance, supervisor, quant, risk and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Regulatory decision ownership | Name who approves corrections, submissions, stand-downs and go-live sign-off before real trade data replaces the snapshot. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Reporting exceptions, documentation gaps and credential status found by manual review Establish the manual reconciliation effort before attributing earlier detection to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Control area | Measurement period | Exceptions found | Evidence source | Owner | Time to resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Compliance business owner | Approve scope, escalation routes and production success measures. |
| Authorized compliance reviewers | Approve staged corrections and submissions before any authenticated ARM transmission. |
| Desk supervisors and Quant Execution | Review proposed stand-downs and training actions, and give algorithm go-live sign-off. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and five skills; confirm saved instructions and Draft state. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any compliance connection is approved. |
| Compliance connection owners | Approve trade data, ARM, learning and Teams access through dedicated, verified least-privilege references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Regress RC-01 through RC-05 on one final revision and resolve the RC-03 and RC-05 discrepancies. |
| Operations owner | Own monitoring, support and configuration recovery; route approvals to authorized reviewers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for compliance have named agreement.
- [ ] The compliance owner records current reporting exceptions, documentation gaps and credential status before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/fs-regulatory-compliance/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and confirm blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The approved environment and publisher prefix for the compliance build are recorded before a build lane is chosen.
- [ ] The customer approves the sign-in requirement, audience and least-privilege scopes for trade and trader data before any connection is bound.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/fs-regulatory-compliance/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/fs-regulatory-compliance/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/fs-regulatory-compliance/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/fs-regulatory-compliance/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name the manual agent
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Locate the default web-search capability
6. Remove default web search
7. Open the knowledge uploader
8. Upload synthetic compliance records
9. Upload rules and controls
10. Verify both knowledge sources
11. Open the SKILL.md uploader
12. Upload compliance dashboard skill
13. Upload trade surveillance skill
14. Upload documentation review skill
15. Upload remediation preparation skill
16. Upload certification readiness skill
17. Open the model picker
18. Select Claude Sonnet 4.6
19. Review instructions, knowledge, skills, and tools
20. Open a fresh Preview conversation
21. Run and verify RC-01 audit readiness
22. Run and verify RC-02 certifications
23. Run and verify RC-03 trade surveillance
24. Run and verify RC-04 algorithm go-live
25. Run and verify RC-05 board evidence
26. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: RC-01, RC-02, RC-03, RC-04, RC-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Step 2-5. Close review gates

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Regress every locked prompt on one final saved revision, resolve the recorded discrepancies and review per-step evidence.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] A fresh saved-state check confirms the instructions, two knowledge files and five skills on the current Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the smoke test calls `FSRegulatoryCompliance` and returns its required markers.
- [ ] All five unchanged locked prompts pass on one final saved revision, judged on facts, routing, citations and safety, not markers alone.
- [ ] Every declared step has freshly captured or personally reviewed evidence; no current capture is reusable yet.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before any trade, trader or algorithm record is shown. Request only the scopes that approved trade, reporting and learning sources need. Restrict the audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Order-management or transaction-reporting data through an approved connector or API

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance connection owners

1. **Bind Order-management or transaction-reporting data through an approved connector or API — read:** Bind read-only trade and reference-data queries through a connector or MCP tool.

2. **Identity for Order-management or transaction-reporting data through an approved connector or API:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Order-management or transaction-reporting data through an approved connector or API:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Order-management or transaction-reporting data through an approved connector or API:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 7](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Stage only the verified execution venue from the source record. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, transmission or enrollment succeeded.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved Reporting Mechanism through Power Automate or a custom connector

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance connection owners

1. **Bind Approved Reporting Mechanism through Power Automate or a custom connector — read-write:** Build an authenticated custom connector that transmits only after reviewer approval.

2. **Identity for Approved Reporting Mechanism through Power Automate or a custom connector:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved Reporting Mechanism through Power Automate or a custom connector:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved Reporting Mechanism through Power Automate or a custom connector:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Stage a synthetic dry run only; transmission needs reviewer approval and an authenticated ARM connector. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, transmission or enrollment succeeded.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Learning management system

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance connection owners

1. **Bind Learning management system — read:** Bind read-only credential records; keep enrollment in the approved learning workflow.

2. **Identity for Learning management system:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Learning management system:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Learning management system:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Refuse the conversion; session dates are not expiry dates. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim that a lookup, transmission or enrollment succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Teams

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams — write:** Gate Teams escalation or approval cards behind authorized reviewers.

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): No legal determination, stand-down or notification; a proposed stand-down goes to supervisor review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Do not stage it; report that the source value is missing.

### Step 3-5. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance connection owners

Create tools for trade data, the reporting mechanism, certification records and Teams through dedicated references; approve before any correction or submission call.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] An explicit approval step precedes any correction or submission call to an external connector.
- [ ] No lookup, transmission, enrollment or notification is reported unless an approved production tool returns success evidence.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test the approved deployment with compliance and denied identities; a maker's working connection does not prove other users' access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic tolerances, cycles and look-ahead windows are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations name the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact compliance assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked compliance corpus | All five cases, RC-01 through RC-05, return every required marker, no forbidden phrase and the minimum word count. |
| Final-revision regression | The recorded review stays blocked until all five prompts pass on one final saved revision. |
| Remediation coverage | An added remediation case shows dry-run labeling and reviewer approval before any ARM wiring. |
| Compliance authority boundary | Any audit prediction, legal advice, transmission, filing, enrollment, notification or record-change claim is no-go. |
| Manual inventory | Saved global instructions, two knowledge files, five skills and the reviewed model are confirmed, with no tools. |
| Release state | The validated pilot agent remains Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Compliance business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation from the approval owner.
- [ ] The approved compliance audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review failed sessions, mislabeled-field answers, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Recovery is rehearsed with a restore path supported for the compliance environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, knowledge use, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
